slides.narration: Look at this town by a river. A car puffs out exhaust, a power plant pours hot water into the river, drains carry sewage, garbage burns in a heap and fertiliser washes off the fields. Each one is a source of pollution. In this part we meet them one by one.

slides.heading: Air pollutants and their sources

rows: Combines with haemoglobin; less oxygen to tissues
Coal-burning power plants, factories, brick kilns
Brick kilns, diesel engines, burning garbage and crop stubble

visual.alt: Table of five air pollutants, their main sources and harmful effects

slides.narration: Most air pollution comes from burning things: fuels in vehicles, coal in power plants and kilns, and garbage in the open. Each burning releases a mixture of gases and fine particles that harm our lungs and the planet.

slides.narration: Think of tiny particles of soot and dust.

slides.heading: Water pollution

rows: Bacteria decomposing it use up oxygen; spreads cholera, typhoid
Phosphates and nitrates cause algal bloom (eutrophication)
Poisons such as mercury and lead build up in fish
Coat birds' feathers; block air exchange at the surface

visual.alt: Table of four water pollutants and their effects

slides.narration: Water carries away whatever we pour into it. Sewage and detergents feed microbes and algae that steal the oxygen fish need. Factory poisons build up in fish. Oil floats as a film that kills birds and blocks air from the water.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: why do fish die below a power plant?
slides.body_md: Water at **20 °C** holds about **9.1** mg of oxygen per litre; at **30 °C**, only about **7.6**.
bullets: Step 1: fall = 9.1 − 7.6 = **1.5** mg per litre.
Step 2: as a percentage of 9.1: about **16.5 per cent** less oxygen.
Step 3: warm fish are more active and need **more** oxygen, so they suffocate: **thermal pollution**.

visual.alt: Worked table: dissolved oxygen falls from 9.1 to 7.6 milligrams per litre when water warms from 20 to 30 degrees

slides.narration: Warm water simply cannot hold as much oxygen as cool water. At the same time, fish in warm water breathe faster and need more. That double blow is why hot water from power plants can empty a river of fish.

slides.heading: Quick check: hot water
slides.body_md: Fill in: hot water from power plants causes ______ pollution.
slides.narration: The word comes from heat.

slides.heading: Soil pollution

rows: Soil becomes acidic or salty; useful organisms die
Do not decay; block air and water; leak poisons

visual.alt: Table of four sources of soil pollution and their effects

slides.narration: Soil is alive with tiny organisms that keep it fertile. Too much fertiliser, persistent pesticides and dumped plastics and metals poison them, so the soil slowly loses its fertility.

slides.heading: Biomedical waste and radiation
slides.body_md: **Biomedical waste** (syringes, needles, dressings, body tissues) can spread infection; it must be **segregated** in colour-coded bins and treated by **autoclaving** or **incineration**. **Radiation** from X-rays, radioactive waste and nuclear accidents can damage genes and cause **cancer**.

rows: Injury; spread of hepatitis and other infections

visual.alt: Table of biomedical waste and radiation sources, their dangers and safe handling

slides.narration: A used needle in an ordinary bin can infect the person who empties it. That is why hospitals sort their waste into separate coloured bins. Radiation is invisible, so X ray rooms use lead shields and radioactive waste is sealed away.

slides.heading: Noise pollution
slides.body_md: Sound is measured in **decibels (dB)**. Long exposure above about **80 dB** can damage hearing.

slides.narration: A library is quiet, a classroom a little louder. But a busy road, a wedding band or a firecracker nearby go well past the harmful level. Loud noise can cause hearing loss, stress, sleeplessness and high blood pressure.

bullets: Step 1: find the harmful line on the chart.
Step 2: list the bars that cross it: Busy road, Wedding band, Firecracker nearby.
Step 3: count them: **3** places; suggest one remedy for each.

rows: No pressure horns; trees as sound barriers

slides.narration: Read the chart against the line, count the bars that cross it, and think of a practical remedy for each. Quieter horns, lower volumes and keeping a safe distance all protect our ears.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Air: carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, carbon dioxide from vehicles, industry, kilns and burning garbage.
Water: sewage, detergents, industrial waste, oil; hot water causes thermal pollution.
Soil: excess fertilisers, pesticides, urban and industrial waste.
Biomedical waste must be segregated; radiation and noise harm health.

visual.alt: Summary table of one key source for each type of pollution

slides.narration: To recap. Burning pollutes the air, waste pollutes water and soil, hospitals must handle their waste with care, and loud noise and radiation harm our health. Knowing the source is the first step to controlling it.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: Pair every pollutant with its **source** and its **effect**.
Thermal pollution works by **lowering dissolved oxygen**.
Biomedical waste: **segregate**, then **autoclave or incinerate**.
Write the unit **decibel (dB)** for noise.
slides.narration: Exam tips. Always link a pollutant to where it comes from and what it does. Explain thermal pollution through oxygen. Say that biomedical waste is segregated and treated. And measure noise in decibels.

slides.heading: Waste, Global Effects and Control
slides.body_md: Part 2 — wastes that stay, problems that cross borders, and what we can do.

visual.alt: Flow: wastes and pesticides, then global effects, then control measures

slides.narration: Some wastes disappear quickly, others stay for centuries. Some pollutants harm the whole planet, warming it, souring its rain and thinning its ozone shield. In this part we look at these problems and at the ways to control them.

slides.heading: Biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes

rows: Broken down by bacteria and fungi
Food scraps, paper, cow dung, leaves
Must be reduced, reused or recycled

visual.alt: Table comparing biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes

slides.narration: A banana peel rots in days because bacteria and fungi feed on it. A plastic bag can lie in the soil for hundreds of years because nothing can digest it. That difference decides how each kind of waste should be handled.

slides.heading: Quick check: why plastics stay
slides.narration: Who breaks down dead matter?

slides.heading: DDT in a food chain
slides.body_md: DDT is **non-biodegradable**. It is stored in body fat and becomes **more concentrated** at each step: **biomagnification**.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: how much does DDT build up?
slides.body_md: Using the imagined values: lake water **0.00002** ppm, fish-eating bird **20** ppm.
bullets: Step 1: divide the higher level by the lower: 20 ÷ 0.00002.
Step 2: the answer is **10,00,000** (ten lakh) times.
Step 3: explain: not broken down, not excreted, and each animal eats many from the level below.

slides.narration: Dividing shows how dramatic biomagnification is. The bird holds about a million times the concentration found in the water. That is why a pesticide sprayed in small amounts can still thin the eggshells of birds of prey.

slides.heading: Controlling pollution

rows: Burns cleanly: less smoke and sulphur dioxide
Limit pollutants from new vehicles (BS-VI in force across India since April 2020)
Switching off engines at red lights
Trees absorb carbon dioxide and trap dust
Clean sewage before it reaches rivers
Less non-biodegradable waste (India: listed items banned from July 2022)
Compost and natural pest control instead of chemicals

visual.alt: Table of seven pollution control measures and how each helps

slides.narration: Every source has a remedy. Cleaner fuels and stricter vehicle norms cut exhaust. Trees soak up gases and dust. Treatment plants clean sewage. Plastic bans and organic farming keep persistent chemicals out of the soil and water.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: auditing a canteen
slides.body_md: A school canteen produced **24 kg** of waste in a day.
bullets: Step 1: biodegradable = food 12 + paper 6 = **18 kg**.
Step 2: share = 18 ÷ 24 × 100 = **75 per cent**.
Step 3: compost the 18 kg; send the other 6 kg (plastic, glass, cans) for recycling.

visual.alt: Worked table of canteen waste: 18 of 24 kilograms is biodegradable

slides.narration: Sort first, then calculate. Three quarters of this canteen’s waste can be turned into compost. The rest should be kept out of the compost pit and sent for recycling. Segregating waste at the source makes both possible.

sections.heading: 1. Air pollution: sources and major pollutants
sections.body_md:
**Pollution** is the addition of harmful substances (**pollutants**) or energy to air, water or soil, making it harmful to living things.

**Sources:** vehicles, industries and power plants, burning of garbage, brick kilns, burning of crop stubble.

| Pollutant | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Carbon monoxide | Incomplete burning in vehicles | Combines with haemoglobin; less oxygen carried; headache, death |
| Sulphur dioxide | Burning coal (power plants, kilns, factories) | Irritates eyes and lungs; acid rain |
| Nitrogen oxides | Vehicles, power plants | Lung damage; acid rain; smog |
| Particulate matter | Kilns, diesel engines, burning garbage and stubble | Coughs, asthma, lung disease; haze |
| Carbon dioxide | Burning fossil fuels and wood | Global warming |

key_terms.definition_md: A substance that makes air, water or soil harmful to living things.
Fine solid particles such as soot and dust suspended in air.

sections.heading: 2. Water, thermal and soil pollution
sections.body_md:
**Water pollution**
- **Domestic sewage:** organic matter decomposed by bacteria that use up **dissolved oxygen**; germs cause cholera, typhoid, jaundice.
- **Detergents** (phosphates) and **fertilisers** (nitrates): cause **eutrophication** (algal bloom); dead algae decay and use up oxygen; fish die.
- **Industrial waste:** poisonous chemicals and heavy metals such as **mercury** and **lead** build up in fish and people.
- **Oil spills:** an oil film coats birds' feathers and cuts off gas exchange between air and water.

**Thermal pollution:** hot water from power plants and industries raises water temperature; warm water holds **less dissolved oxygen** (about 9.1 mg per litre at 20 °C but about 7.6 at 30 °C), so fish and other aquatic life suffer.

**Soil pollution:** excess chemical **fertilisers** and **pesticides**, **urban waste** (plastics, metals, e-waste), industrial waste and acid rain; soil loses fertility and its organisms.

key_terms.definition_md: Excessive growth of algae due to nutrients such as phosphates and nitrates.
Harmful warming of water bodies by hot water from industry.

sections.heading: 3. Biomedical waste, radiation and noise pollution
sections.body_md:
**Biomedical waste:** used syringes, needles, dressings, body tissues and expired medicines from hospitals and clinics. It can spread infections (such as hepatitis) and injure waste handlers, so it must be **segregated at source** into colour-coded containers (for example, sharps in puncture-proof containers, as under India's Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016) and treated by **autoclaving**, **incineration** or other approved methods.

**Radiation pollution:** sources include X-rays, radioactive waste from nuclear power plants, nuclear accidents and nuclear tests. Effects: damage to genes (mutations), **cancer**, burns, harm to unborn babies. Protection: lead shielding, safe storage of radioactive waste.

**Noise pollution:** unwanted, loud sound measured in **decibels (dB)**. Sources: vehicle horns and traffic, loudspeakers, firecrackers, aircraft, factories and construction. Long exposure above about **80 dB** can damage hearing. Effects: **hearing loss**, stress, irritability, sleeplessness, high blood pressure.

key_terms.definition_md: Waste from hospitals and clinics that may carry infection.
Unit used to measure the loudness of sound.

sections.heading: 4. Biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes; DDT
sections.body_md:
| Biodegradable | Non-biodegradable |
|---|---|
| Broken down by bacteria and fungi | Not broken down by decomposers |
| Food scraps, paper, cow dung, leaves | Plastics, glass, metals, DDT |
| Can be composted | Must be reduced, reused, recycled |

**DDT** is a **non-biodegradable** (persistent) pesticide. It is not broken down or excreted and is stored in body fat. As each animal eats many from the level below, DDT becomes more **concentrated at each step** of the food chain: **biological magnification**. Top consumers such as fish-eating birds are harmed most (for example, thin eggshells that break). Many countries, including India, have banned or restricted its use in farming.

key_terms.definition_md: Can be broken down by decomposers.
Increase in concentration of a persistent chemical along a food chain.

sections.heading: 5. Greenhouse effect, global warming, acid rain and ozone depletion
sections.body_md:
**Greenhouse effect:** carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs and water vapour let sunlight through but **trap heat** given off by the Earth. More of these gases (from burning fuels, deforestation, paddy fields and cattle) cause **global warming**: melting glaciers and polar ice, rising sea levels, extreme weather, harm to crops and wildlife.

**Acid rain:** **sulphur dioxide** and **nitrogen oxides** dissolve in rain water to form **sulphuric and nitric acids** (rain more acidic than its normal pH of about 5.6). Effects: acidic lakes (fish die), damaged forests and soils, corroded **marble** and metal.

**Ozone depletion:** the **ozone layer** in the **stratosphere** absorbs most harmful **UV rays**. **CFCs** from old refrigerators, air conditioners and sprays release chlorine, which destroys ozone (an "ozone hole" was found over Antarctica in the 1980s). More UV-B causes **skin cancer**, **cataract**, weaker immunity and harm to crops and plankton. Under the **Montreal Protocol (1987)** countries agreed to phase out CFCs.

sections.heading: 6. Control measures and the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan
sections.body_md:
- **CNG** (compressed natural gas) for buses and autos: burns cleanly.
- **Bharat Stage (BS) emission norms:** Government of India standards limiting vehicle pollutants; **BS-VI** has applied across India since **April 2020** (as of 2026).
- **Switching off engines** at long red lights; using public transport.
- **Social forestry:** planting trees on community land to absorb carbon dioxide and trap dust.
- **Sewage treatment plants** before discharge into rivers; cooling of hot water before release.
- **Bans on plastics:** India banned a list of single-use plastic items from **1 July 2022**; many states have their own bans.
- **Organic farming:** compost and biological pest control instead of chemical fertilisers and pesticides.

**Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** (Clean India Mission), launched on **2 October 2014**. Aims: a clean India; an end to **open defecation** through toilets; **scientific solid-waste management** (segregation, composting, recycling); a change in people's habits about cleanliness.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Mixing up the greenhouse effect (heat trapped) and ozone depletion (UV let in).
- Naming carbon dioxide as the cause of acid rain (it is sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides).
- Saying thermal pollution poisons fish (it lowers dissolved oxygen).
- Calling paper non-biodegradable, or DDT biodegradable.
- Giving dates for schemes and norms that are not asked; when you do, use the ones above.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1 mark: a term, a pollutant, an odd one out **with its category**.
- 2 marks: a source and its effect, or two measures.
- 3 marks: formation and effects of acid rain, a labelled greenhouse diagram, or three control measures with reasons.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Carbon monoxide, Sulphur dioxide, Nitrogen dioxide, Oxygen.

answer.model_answer_md: **Oxygen**; the others are **air pollutants**.

questions.solution_md: Oxygen is a normal part of clean air.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: a person can be poisoned by carbon monoxide without noticing it.

answer.model_answer_md: Carbon monoxide is **colourless and odourless**, so it cannot be seen or smelt while it **binds to haemoglobin**.

questions.solution_md: Colourless, odourless.

questions.stem_md: Name two pollutants released by vehicles and state one harmful effect of each.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Carbon monoxide:** combines with haemoglobin and reduces oxygen supply, causing headache and even death.
2. **Nitrogen oxides:** irritate the lungs and help form **acid rain** and smog.

questions.solution_md: Two pollutants with effects.

questions.stem_md: Phosphates from detergents entering a pond lead to

options.text_md: a rise in the temperature of the water
rapid growth of algae, which later die and use up the oxygen in the water
the thinning of the ozone layer

questions.solution_md: Phosphates are nutrients for algae; their decay uses up oxygen (eutrophication) — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Untreated sewage flowing into a river harms fish mainly because

options.text_md: it makes the water too hot
bacteria decomposing it use up the dissolved oxygen

questions.solution_md: Decomposers break down the organic matter and consume much of the dissolved oxygen — option (b).

questions.stem_md: An oil spill at sea kills many sea birds mainly because the oil

options.text_md: makes the sea water too salty
coats their feathers, so they cannot fly, float or keep warm
raises the temperature of the sea

questions.solution_md: Oiled feathers lose their waterproofing and insulation — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A power plant pours its hot cooling water into a river, and fish downstream begin to die. The main reason is that

options.text_md: warm water holds less dissolved oxygen
fish cannot see in warm water

questions.solution_md: Oxygen is less soluble in warm water, while fish need more of it as they become more active — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Factory waste containing mercury is especially dangerous when it is dumped into the sea because

options.text_md: mercury collects in fish and passes to the people who eat them
mercury quickly breaks down into harmless salts
mercury makes the water too warm for fish
mercury adds oxygen to the water

questions.solution_md: Mercury is not broken down and builds up in food chains; it damages the nervous system of people who eat contaminated fish — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Thermal pollution can reduce the number of fish in a river.

**Reason (R):** Power plants use large amounts of water to cool their machines.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but using water for cooling does not by itself explain fish deaths; the cause is that the warmed water holds less oxygen — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** An oil spill increases the amount of oxygen in sea water.

**Reason (R):** A layer of oil on the surface cuts off the exchange of gases between the air and the water.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is false: the oil layer lowers the oxygen in the water. The reason is true — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Discharge of hot water from power plants into rivers causes ______ pollution.
questions.solution_md: Thermal pollution.

questions.stem_md: Give the term: the excessive growth of algae in a lake fed with nutrients from fertilisers or detergents.

answer.model_answer_md: **Eutrophication** (algal bloom).

questions.solution_md: Eutrophication.

questions.stem_md: What is thermal pollution? State its effect on aquatic life.

answer.model_answer_md: Thermal pollution is the **warming of a water body** by hot water released from power plants and factories. Warm water holds **less dissolved oxygen**, so fish and other aquatic animals **suffocate or die**, and their breeding is disturbed.

questions.solution_md: Definition; less oxygen.

questions.stem_md: Name two sources of soil pollution and state one harmful effect of each.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Excess chemical fertilisers:** make the soil acidic or salty and kill useful soil organisms.
2. **Urban waste** such as plastics: does not decay, blocks water and air in the soil and releases harmful chemicals.

questions.solution_md: Two sources with effects.

questions.stem_md: Used syringes and blood-soaked bandages from a clinic should be

options.text_md: collected in separate colour-coded containers and treated, for example by autoclaving or incineration

questions.solution_md: Biomedical waste can spread infection, so it is segregated at source and treated safely — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Long exposure to radiation from radioactive substances can cause
questions.solution_md: Radiation damages DNA, which can lead to mutations and cancer — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which of these is a harmful effect of continuous loud noise?

options.text_md: Loss of hearing, stress and high blood pressure

questions.solution_md: Loud noise damages the ear and raises stress and blood pressure — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Study the chart. How many of the places have sound levels above about 80 dB, the level taken as harmful with long exposure?
questions.solution_md: Busy road (85), Wedding band (100), Firecracker nearby (125) are above 80 dB: 3 places — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Biomedical waste must be kept separate from ordinary household waste.

**Reason (R):** Hospitals produce large quantities of waste every day.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but the amount is not the reason; it must be separated because it can carry infection and injure people — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** X-ray technicians wear lead aprons while at work.

**Reason (R):** X-rays are a form of noise pollution.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true: lead shields the body from radiation. The reason is false: X-rays are radiation, not noise — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The loudness (intensity) of sound is measured in ______.
questions.solution_md: Decibels (dB).

questions.stem_md: Give the term: waste such as used syringes, dressings and body tissues produced in hospitals and clinics.

answer.model_answer_md: **Biomedical waste.**

questions.solution_md: Biomedical waste.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: used needles from hospitals are collected in separate puncture-proof containers.

answer.model_answer_md: To prevent **injury and the spread of infections** such as hepatitis to cleaners and waste pickers.

questions.solution_md: Prevents injury and infection.

questions.stem_md: Name two sources of noise pollution and two effects of loud noise on human health.

answer.model_answer_md: Sources: **vehicle horns and traffic**; **loudspeakers and firecrackers**. Effects: **loss of hearing**; **stress, sleeplessness and high blood pressure**.

questions.solution_md: Two sources; two effects.

questions.stem_md: Which of these wastes is biodegradable?
questions.solution_md: Bacteria and fungi decompose vegetable matter; the others are not broken down — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Plastics are called non-biodegradable because

options.text_md: decomposers such as bacteria and fungi cannot break them down

questions.solution_md: Without decomposition, plastics stay in the environment for very long times — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Study the figure. The fish-eating bird has the highest level of DDT in the food chain because

options.text_md: birds drink more lake water than fish
DDT is made inside the body of the bird
DDT is not broken down and builds up at each step of the food chain
birds are sprayed directly with DDT

questions.solution_md: Each animal eats many from the level below and stores their DDT, so it is concentrated upwards — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** DDT harms fish-eating birds more than the plankton in the same lake.

**Reason (R):** DDT is a non-biodegradable pesticide that becomes more concentrated at each level of a food chain.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and biomagnification of the persistent DDT is why the top consumers carry the most — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Give the term: the increase in the concentration of a non-biodegradable chemical at each level of a food chain.

answer.model_answer_md: **Biological magnification** (biomagnification).

questions.solution_md: Biomagnification.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Fruit peels, Paper, Cow dung, Plastic bottle.

answer.model_answer_md: **Plastic bottle**; the others are **biodegradable wastes**.

questions.solution_md: Plastic is non-biodegradable.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: DDT sprayed in small amounts on fields can still harm eagles and other birds of prey.

answer.model_answer_md: DDT is **not broken down**; it becomes **more concentrated at each step** of the food chain (biomagnification), so top predators get the highest dose.

questions.solution_md: Biomagnification.

marking_scheme.step: Persistent and magnified up the chain

questions.stem_md: Distinguish between biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes, giving one example of each.

answer.model_answer_md: **Biodegradable** wastes are broken down by **bacteria and fungi** into harmless substances, for example **vegetable peels**. **Non-biodegradable** wastes are **not broken down** by decomposers and remain for a long time, for example **polythene bags**.

questions.solution_md: Decomposition; examples.

questions.stem_md: Which gas released by burning coal, petrol and wood adds most to the greenhouse effect?
questions.solution_md: Carbon dioxide from burning fuels traps heat radiated by the Earth — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Acid rain is caused mainly by

options.text_md: sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolving in rain water

questions.solution_md: These gases form sulphuric and nitric acids in the clouds — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which of these can release chemicals that deplete the ozone layer?

options.text_md: Old refrigerators and air conditioners that use CFCs

questions.solution_md: CFCs leaking from old cooling machines and sprays rise to the stratosphere and destroy ozone — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Over many years, the marble of an old monument near an oil refinery turned yellowish and pitted. The most likely cause is

options.text_md: thermal pollution of a nearby river
acid rain formed from sulphur dioxide released by the refinery

questions.solution_md: Sulphur dioxide forms acid rain, which reacts with the calcium carbonate of marble — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Normal rain has a pH of about 5.6. A sample of acid rain has a pH of 4.6. Each drop of one pH unit makes a liquid ten times more acidic. How many times more acidic is the sample?
questions.solution_md: The pH falls from 5.6 to 4.6, which is one unit; one unit lower = 10 times more acidic.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Without any greenhouse gases, the Earth would be much colder than it is.

**Reason (R):** Greenhouse gases trap part of the heat given off by the Earth.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the trapping of heat by these gases is what keeps the Earth warm enough for life — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Depletion of the ozone layer increases the number of cases of skin cancer.

**Reason (R):** Depletion of the ozone layer makes rain acidic.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true: more UV-B reaches the ground. The reason is false: acid rain comes from sulphur and nitrogen oxides — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Chlorofluorocarbons, or ______, once used in refrigerators and sprays, deplete the ozone layer.
questions.solution_md: CFCs.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Carbon dioxide, Methane, Nitrous oxide, Oxygen.

answer.model_answer_md: **Oxygen**; the others are **greenhouse gases**.

questions.solution_md: Oxygen does not trap heat significantly.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: fish disappear from lakes downwind of coal-burning power plants.

answer.model_answer_md: Sulphur dioxide from the plants forms **acid rain**, which makes the **lake water acidic**, killing fish and their eggs.

questions.solution_md: Acid rain acidifies lakes.

questions.stem_md: Explain how acid rain is formed and state two of its harmful effects.

answer.model_answer_md: Burning coal and petrol releases **sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides**. In the clouds these dissolve in water droplets to form **sulphuric acid and nitric acid**, which fall as acid rain. Effects: it makes **lakes acidic**, killing fish, and it **damages trees** and **corrodes marble** buildings.

questions.solution_md: Formation; two effects.

questions.stem_md: Draw a labelled diagram to show the greenhouse effect.

answer.model_answer_md: The Sun with arrows of **sunlight** passing through a layer of **greenhouse gases** to the Earth; arrows of **heat (infrared)** going up from the Earth, most **reflected back** by the gas layer and a few **escaping** to space.

questions.solution_md: Labelled diagram.

marking_scheme.step: Sunlight reaching the Earth through the gas layer

questions.stem_md: Public buses in Delhi were switched to CNG mainly because

options.text_md: CNG gives buses a higher top speed
CNG burns more cleanly, giving out far less smoke and sulphur dioxide than diesel
CNG removes carbon dioxide from the air

questions.solution_md: Compressed natural gas burns almost completely and has little sulphur — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Bharat Stage emission norms are

options.text_md: rules for disposing of hospital waste
standards set by the Government of India that limit the pollutants a vehicle may release

questions.solution_md: BS norms limit exhaust pollutants such as carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and particles — option (d).

questions.stem_md: The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, launched by the Government of India in October 2014, aims mainly to

options.text_md: make India clean, end open defecation and improve the handling of solid waste

questions.solution_md: The mission focuses on toilets, cleanliness and waste management — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Plastic bags can safely be thrown into rivers because they float away.

**Reason (R):** Plastic bags are non-biodegradable.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is false: plastics choke animals and block drains wherever they go. The reason is true — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Before it is released into a river, sewage should be cleaned in a sewage ______ plant.
questions.solution_md: Sewage treatment plant.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Social forestry, Use of CNG, Sewage treatment, Open burning of garbage.

answer.model_answer_md: **Open burning of garbage**; the others are **measures to control pollution**.

questions.solution_md: Open burning causes pollution.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: drivers are advised to switch off their engines at long red lights.

answer.model_answer_md: An idling engine **burns fuel and releases exhaust** without moving; switching off **saves fuel and reduces air pollution**.

questions.solution_md: Saves fuel; less exhaust.

marking_scheme.step: Less fuel burnt and less exhaust

questions.stem_md: State two aims of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. To **end open defecation** by building and using toilets in homes, schools and public places.
2. To keep streets and public places clean through **scientific collection and disposal of solid waste**, and to change people's habits about cleanliness.

questions.solution_md: Two aims.

questions.stem_md: Suggest three measures to reduce air pollution in a crowded city, and say how each helps.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. Run buses and autos on **CNG** and enforce **Bharat Stage** norms: vehicles give out less smoke and gas.
2. **Switch off engines** at long red lights and use public transport: less fuel is burnt.
3. Plant trees by **social forestry**: trees absorb carbon dioxide and trap dust.

questions.solution_md: Three measures with reasons.

questions.passage_md: A lake near farmland was found to contain traces of DDT washed in from sprayed fields. Scientists measured the DDT in living things of the lake (imagined values, in parts per million): lake water 0.00002; plankton 0.04; small fish 0.5; large fish 2; fish-eating bird 20. Fish-eating birds nesting by the lake were laying eggs with thin shells that broke easily.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** **Biological magnification** (biomagnification).

A river flows past a power plant and then past a town. Students tested the water at two points:

| Place | Temperature | Dissolved oxygen (mg per litre) |
|---|---|---|
| Above the power plant | 20 °C | 9.1 |
| Just below the plant's outlet | 30 °C | 7.6 |

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** **Thermal pollution.**

**(b)** 16.5 %

**(c)** Warm water holds **less dissolved oxygen**, while fish in warm water become **more active** and need **more oxygen**. They may **suffocate**, and their eggs may fail to develop.

**(d)** Untreated **sewage** from the drains adds **organic matter**. **Bacteria** decomposing it use up the **dissolved oxygen**, so fish die, and decay without oxygen releases **foul-smelling gases**.

**(e)** 1. The power plant should **cool its water** in cooling towers or ponds before release.
2. The town should build a **sewage treatment plant** so that only treated water enters the river.
3. **Ban dumping** of garbage and factory waste into the river, and plant trees along its banks.

**(b)** Fall: 9.1 − 7.6 gives 1.5 mg per litre. Percentage fall: $\dfrac{1.5}{9.1} \times 100 \approx 16.5$ per cent.

**(c)** Less oxygen, more demand.

**(d)** Sewage decay uses oxygen.

**(e)** Three measures.

children.stem_md: Which letter shows a source of thermal pollution?

answer.model_answer_md: **B** (hot water from the power plant).

children.stem_md: State two effects of the waste from C on the river and on people.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. Its **organic matter** is decomposed by bacteria that use up **dissolved oxygen**, so fish die.
2. It carries **germs** that spread **water-borne diseases** such as cholera and typhoid among people who use the water.

children.stem_md: Explain why green patches appear in the river near E.

answer.model_answer_md: Rain washes **fertilisers** from the fields into the river. Their **nitrates and phosphates** act as nutrients, so **algae grow rapidly** and form green patches: **eutrophication** (algal bloom).

children.stem_md: Why is the activity at D harmful?

answer.model_answer_md: Burning garbage, especially **plastics**, releases **smoke, soot and poisonous gases** into the air. These cause **breathing problems** and some gases can cause **cancer**.

children.stem_md: **Either** (i): Suggest one control measure each for the sources A, C and D.

answer.model_answer_md:
**A:** use **CNG** or vehicles that meet **Bharat Stage** norms, and switch off engines at red lights.
**C:** treat the sewage in a **sewage treatment plant** before it enters the river.
**D:** **segregate** waste, **compost** the biodegradable part and send the rest for recycling instead of burning it.

alternatives.stem_md: **Or** (ii): Classify the five sources as causing mainly air pollution or mainly water pollution, and name the one that also harms soil.

answer.model_answer_md: **Air pollution:** A (vehicle exhaust) and D (burning garbage). **Water pollution:** B (hot water), C (sewage) and E (fertiliser run-off). **E** also harms **soil**, since excess fertiliser changes its chemistry and kills soil organisms.

alternatives.solution_md: Air: A, D; water: B, C, E; soil: E.

questions.stem_md: Study the figure and answer the questions.
questions.passage_md: In the 1980s scientists found that the ozone layer over Antarctica had become very thin each spring, forming an "ozone hole". The main cause was CFCs from refrigerators, air conditioners and spray cans. Under an international agreement, the Montreal Protocol of 1987, countries agreed to phase out CFCs, and the ozone layer has since begun to recover slowly.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The **stratosphere.**

**(b)** CFCs are very stable, so they **rise slowly** to the stratosphere. There **ultraviolet light** breaks them down, releasing **chlorine**, which **breaks down ozone** molecules; one chlorine atom can destroy many.

**(c)** 1. More cases of **skin cancer** and **cataract** (clouding of the eye lens) in humans.
2. **Damage to crops** and to **plankton** in the sea, which harms food chains.

**(d)** CFCs released **anywhere** spread through the **whole atmosphere**, and the ozone layer protects the **whole Earth**. Only if **all countries** stopped using CFCs could the damage be halted.

**(e)** 1. **Cause:** ozone depletion is caused mainly by **CFCs**; the greenhouse effect is increased mainly by **carbon dioxide** and methane.
2. **Place:** ozone depletion happens in the **stratosphere**; heat is trapped in the **lower atmosphere**.
3. **Effect:** ozone depletion lets in more **UV rays** (skin cancer); the greenhouse effect causes **global warming**.

questions.solution_md:
**(a)** Stratosphere.

**(b)** Chlorine from CFCs destroys ozone.

**(c)** Two effects.

**(d)** Global problem.

**(e)** Cause, place, effect.
